description: Bruno Oger's two-star restaurant in Le Cannet is the most serious gastronomic address in the Cannes luxury catchment. Set in an 18th-century Provençal villa above the Croisette, it combines classical precision, Mediterranean produce and polished destination-restaurant service. It is the table to book when Cannes requires quiet ceremony rather than beachfront theatre.
highlights: Two-Michelin-star Bruno Oger restaurant in a secluded Provençal villa ten minutes above Cannes.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau 2026; Relais & Châteaux; Official restaurant website

description: La Palme d'Or is Cannes' palace fine-dining emblem, now framed by Jean Imbert's cinematic, Mediterranean-facing vision at Hôtel Martinez. The room looks directly onto the Croisette and leans into the glamour of the Film Festival without losing the discipline expected of a Michelin-starred table. It remains the strongest in-city fine-dining booking for visitors staying on the seafront.
highlights: Michelin-starred modern cuisine at Hôtel Martinez with Croisette views and cinema-inspired Riviera glamour.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau 2026; Hyatt Hotel Martinez; Official restaurant website

description: Louroc gives Cannes-based diners access to the mythic Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc in a polished Michelin-starred format. The cooking is Mediterranean and Provençal, built around the region's best artisans and served with sunset views over the sea. Though in Cap d'Antibes, it is one of the rare outside-city restaurants that clearly belongs in the Cannes luxury conversation.
highlights: Michelin-starred Riviera fine dining at the legendary Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc with dramatic sea views.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Oetker Collection; Antibes Juan-les-Pins Tourism; Official hotel website

description: Mareluna is a refined seaside Michelin-starred restaurant at Château de Théoule, within the western Cannes catchment. Francesco Fezza's Mediterranean cooking is elegant, seasonal and framed by one of the area's most cinematic water-facing hotel settings. It is a natural special-occasion alternative for diners who want a coastal drive rather than another Croisette room.
highlights: Michelin-starred Mediterranean cuisine in a seaside château setting west of Cannes.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Château de Théoule; Official restaurant website

description: L'Or Bleu is a Michelin-starred cliffside restaurant at Tiara Miramar, facing the Mediterranean from Théoule-sur-Mer. Its creative Mediterranean menu, formal service and grand terrace make it a persuasive destination for Cannes guests seeking a quieter Riviera escape. The setting is more resort-like than urban, but the cooking is serious enough to justify the journey.
highlights: One-star creative Mediterranean cuisine on a dramatic hotel terrace above the sea in Théoule-sur-Mer.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Tiara Miramar Beach Resort; Official restaurant website

description: La Passagère is the glamorous Michelin-starred dining room of Hôtel Belles Rives in Juan-les-Pins. The terrace faces the Lérins Islands and the cooking gives seafood and local produce a luminous, highly composed treatment. It is slightly outside Cannes proper, but the historic hotel setting and star-level cuisine make it highly relevant to the Riviera luxury diner.
highlights: Michelin-starred seafood-led cuisine with a Belle Époque terrace looking toward the Lérins Islands.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Hôtel Belles Rives; Official restaurant website

description: Les Pêcheurs is a Michelin-starred Mediterranean seafood restaurant at Cap d'Antibes Beach Hotel. Its glass-fronted dining room and terrace frame the coastline while Nicolas Rondelli's cooking keeps the focus on the sea. For Cannes-based diners, it is a polished alternative to the Croisette with a more intimate resort rhythm.
highlights: One-star Mediterranean seafood at Cap d'Antibes Beach Hotel with wide sea views.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Relais & Châteaux; Cap d'Antibes Beach Hotel; Official restaurant website

description: Bessem brings a refined one-star dining room to Mandelieu-La Napoule, just west of Cannes. Chef Bessem Ben Abdallah's Mediterranean cuisine is technically assured, calm and personal, served in a leafy town-house setting. It is less showy than the beachfront addresses, but for culinary seriousness it deserves a place in the Cannes catchment.
highlights: Michelin-starred Mediterranean restaurant in a quiet, garden-like Mandelieu setting.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Mandelieu-La Napoule Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Les Terraillers is a Michelin-starred restaurant in a 16th-century pottery in Biot, included here as one of the strongest close-outskirts gastronomic tables available to Cannes diners. Michaël Fulci's cooking is modern, Southern and product-led, with a more composed register than many Riviera resort restaurants. The address rewards guests who want architecture, calm and serious technique in one evening.
highlights: One-star modern Southern cuisine in a historic 16th-century pottery near Cannes and Antibes.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau 2026; Official restaurant website

description: La Bastide Saint-Antoine is Jacques Chibois' long-established Grasse destination, set in a Provençal country house and garden above the perfume capital. It no longer needs a current star to remain one of the Riviera's most established luxury-country dining experiences. For Cannes guests, it works best as a deliberate countryside dinner rather than a spontaneous central booking.
highlights: Historic Provençal destination restaurant in a country bastide and garden above Grasse.
sources: Michelin Guide; Gault&Millau 2026; Official restaurant website

description: Amarines brings Mauro Colagreco's Riviera luxury vocabulary to Villa Miraé in Cap d'Antibes. The restaurant is more gastronomic and intimate than the hotel's all-day terrace, emphasizing vegetables, sustainable fishing and a polished coastal rhythm. It is an important new-generation alternative for Cannes diners who follow chef-led Riviera projects.
highlights: Mauro Colagreco-led gastronomic dining at Villa Miraé with a produce-led Mediterranean identity.
sources: Michelin Guide; Villa Miraé; Mauro Colagreco Restaurants; Official restaurant website

description: La Table du Chef is a compact Cannes restaurant built around a seasonal blind menu and an open-kitchen rhythm. It is more personal and intimate than the city's big social restaurants, with enough culinary seriousness to justify a place in the high-end core. It is best for diners who value a chef-led evening over Croisette spectacle.
highlights: Small chef-led Cannes dining room with an evening blind menu, local produce and open-kitchen intimacy.
sources: Michelin Guide; Gault&Millau; Official restaurant website; Eater

description: Table 22 is one of Cannes' most reliable serious dining rooms outside the palace-hotel circuit. Noël Mantel cooks contemporary Provençal food with seasonal local produce and a wine list that feels unusually personal for a central Cannes restaurant. Its Le Suquet position makes it both accessible and rooted in the old-town dining culture.
highlights: Chef-driven Provençal dining in Le Suquet with a strong wine list and loyal local following.
sources: Michelin Guide; Gault&Millau 2026; Eater; Official restaurant website

description: La Place de Mougins is a polished village-square restaurant in one of the most gastronomically resonant hill towns above Cannes. Its modern cuisine, menus and serious cellar make it a credible alternative to a formal city dinner while keeping the charm of old Mougins. The restaurant is particularly relevant for visitors who want a refined hill-village evening without losing culinary ambition.
highlights: Refined modern cuisine and a serious wine cellar on the historic Mougins village square.
sources: Michelin Guide; Gault&Millau 2026; Official restaurant website

description: Le Figuier de Saint-Esprit remains one of Antibes' most important gastronomic restaurants, tucked into the old town near the ramparts. The cooking is regional, polished and special-occasion minded, with a sense of Riviera tradition rather than beach-club spectacle. It is included as a strong close-catchment address for Cannes diners willing to cross to Antibes for dinner.
highlights: Established Antibes gastronomic restaurant with regional cuisine near the old-town ramparts.
sources: Michelin Guide; Official restaurant website; Riviera dining guides

description: Maison de Bacon is a revived Cap d'Antibes seafood institution with a luxury view and a high-spend Riviera clientele. The kitchen centers on fish, shellfish and wood-grilled seafood, now presented with more contemporary polish. It is one of the strongest non-starred seafood alternatives within a realistic Cannes dinner radius.
highlights: Luxury Cap d'Antibes seafood institution with panoramic sea views and wood-grilled fish.
sources: Michelin Guide; Gault&Millau 2026; Official restaurant website

description: Riviera is the grand palace brasserie of the restored Carlton Cannes, directly on the Croisette. It offers Mediterranean seafood, polished classics and the kind of service rhythm that works for business dinners, film-festival tables and elegant hotel guests. The food is not positioned as tasting-menu fine dining, but the room is central to affluent Cannes.
highlights: Carlton Cannes palace brasserie with Croisette views, seafood classics and polished service.
sources: Gault&Millau 2026; Michelin Guide; Carlton Cannes; Official restaurant website

description: La Maréa is a polished seafood restaurant in Théoule-sur-Mer, looking toward the red-rock coastline west of Cannes. It has the high-end seaside tone, product focus and wine-led rhythm that make it a persuasive alternative to a city brasserie. The address is best for guests who want Riviera seafood with a more discreet coastal mood.
highlights: Upscale seafood restaurant in Théoule-sur-Mer with a refined coastal setting near Cannes.
sources: Michelin Guide; Official restaurant website; Côte d'Azur dining guides

description: La Guérite is Cannes' iconic boat-access island restaurant and beach-club address on Île Sainte-Marguerite. It has operated in some form since 1902 and now blends Mediterranean cooking, yacht arrivals, music and a highly international summer crowd. It is more social and theatrical than gastronomic, but it is essential to Cannes' affluent seaside dining culture.
highlights: Boat-access island beach club and Mediterranean restaurant on Île Sainte-Marguerite, with a see-and-be-seen Riviera crowd.
sources: Official restaurant website; Condé Nast Traveler; Forbes; Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur Tourism

description: Tetou's return to Pointe Croisette has made it one of Cannes' most watched seafood bookings. The revived institution traces its story to 1918 and is built around bouillabaisse, lobster and an expensive, highly visible Riviera dining room. It is the strongest high-end Cannes seafood address for guests who want local mythology and scene in the same reservation.
highlights: Legendary bouillabaisse and seafood institution revived at Pointe Croisette as a major see-and-be-seen address.
sources: Tétou official website; Eater; Nice-Matin; Cannes Tourism

description: Zuma Cannes anchors the new public restaurant mix at Palm Beach with a polished Japanese izakaya format. Floor-to-ceiling windows, a robata kitchen and coastal views make it one of the most internationally recognizable dinner rooms in the city. While it is a global concept, this location clearly passes the Cannes instead-of-Michelin test for affluent social dining.
highlights: Palm Beach Japanese izakaya with robata cooking, coastal views and international luxury-dining pull.
sources: Eater; Official restaurant website; Palm Beach Cannes coverage

description: NAMMOS brings its Mykonos-born beach-club vocabulary to the Croisette at Palm Beach. The Cannes address is built around refined coastal cuisine, music, sunset dining and high-energy Riviera hospitality. It is included as a true beach-club restaurant rather than as a generic waterfront venue.
highlights: Palm Beach beach-club restaurant with Mediterranean glamour, coastal cuisine, music and sunset energy.
sources: Official restaurant website; Luxsure; Palm Beach Cannes coverage

description: Carlton Beach Club is one of the Croisette's defining private-beach dining experiences, attached to the revived Carlton Cannes. It is more about Riviera ritual, address and service than technical gastronomy, but it is essential to how affluent guests actually dine by the sea in Cannes.
highlights: Historic Carlton private beach with Mediterranean dining, sunbeds, sea-facing service and classic Croisette glamour.
sources: Carlton Cannes official website; Cannes Tourism; Excellence Riviera

description: Ciro's Cannes is the Majestic's private-beach seafood restaurant, translating the historic Deauville name into a Riviera yacht-club mood. It combines refined fish and seafood, teak sunbeds and Barrière-style seaside service directly on the Croisette. The beach infrastructure and serious restaurant positioning make it a legitimate Beach club entry.
highlights: Majestic private-beach restaurant with refined seafood, seaside service and yacht-club styling.
sources: Official restaurant website; Hôtel Barrière Le Majestic Cannes; Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur Tourism; MoneyWeek

description: La Môme Plage is the seaside extension of one of Cannes' most recognizable high-end social dining brands. The Croisette beach restaurant pairs refined Mediterranean dishes, sushi, dinner service, valet parking and sunbed culture. It is seasonal in spirit and best understood as a glamorous Cannes beach-club dinner rather than a pure culinary destination.
highlights: Exclusive Croisette beach restaurant with Mediterranean cuisine, sushi, dinner service and sunbed hospitality.
sources: Official restaurant website; Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur Tourism; Riviera dining coverage

description: Fouquet's Cannes is the grand Barrière brasserie on the Croisette, shaped by the Parisian Fouquet's template and the hotel-palace clientele of Le Majestic. The menu leans into brasserie luxury, caviar, truffle, seafood and polished comfort classics. It is not a destination tasting menu, but it is an obvious affluent dinner room in Cannes proper.
highlights: Croisette palace brasserie at Le Majestic with Pierre Gagnaire-linked luxury classics and film-festival relevance.
sources: Gault&Millau 2026; Hôtel Barrière Le Majestic Cannes; Condé Nast Traveler; Official hotel website

description: Beefbar Cannes is the new premium meat-focused address at Hôtel Barrière Le Majestic on the Croisette. The Monaco-born luxury steakhouse format brings international recognition, polished service and a high-spend social dining proposition to one of the city's most visible hotel addresses. It is included because this specific flagship location is clearly positioned for Cannes' affluent dinner market.
highlights: New Croisette Beefbar at Le Majestic, bringing a premium international steakhouse format to Cannes.
sources: Official restaurant website; The Glass Magazine; Eater; Hôtel Barrière Le Majestic Cannes

description: La Petite Maison Cannes brings the luxury Niçoise-Mediterranean brand to Palm Beach with a sea-facing resort setting. The menu's olive oil, seafood, vegetables and Côte d'Azur signatures are familiar to international regulars, while the Cannes location adds panoramic coastal views. It is a strong high-end social dinner option for guests who want Riviera ease over Michelin formality.
highlights: Palm Beach Mediterranean restaurant with La Petite Maison's Riviera repertoire and panoramic sea views.
sources: Official restaurant website; Cannes Tourism; Palm Beach Cannes coverage

description: La Môme Cannes is a central, polished Mediterranean restaurant that has become part of the city's affluent social-dining circuit. The cooking is generous, contemporary and built for sharing, while the room carries the theatrical energy expected around rue Florian. It is a credible instead-of-Michelin choice when the brief is glamour, cocktails, dinner and a lively adult crowd.
highlights: Fashionable rue Florian Mediterranean restaurant with polished service, cocktails and a lively Riviera crowd.
sources: Eater; Official restaurant website; Riviera dining coverage

description: L'Amandier de Mougins is an elegant hill-village restaurant with deep local history, originally associated with Roger Vergé's Mougins legacy. Its terraces, wine list and Provençal-Mediterranean cuisine give Cannes guests a refined but less formal village-night option. It is included as a high-end casual classic rather than as a contemporary Michelin substitute.
highlights: Historic Mougins restaurant with panoramic terraces, Provençal-Mediterranean cooking and a serious cellar.
sources: Gault&Millau 2026; Michelin Guide; Official restaurant website

description: Astoux et Brun is the kind of seafood institution Cannes regulars know to keep in rotation. It is more democratic than the palace restaurants, but its oysters, shellfish and central energy make it culturally important to the city. For affluent diners, it is a relaxed local classic for the night when seafood and people-watching matter more than white-tablecloth ritual.
highlights: Long-running central Cannes seafood institution for oysters, shellfish and a lively local dining rhythm.
sources: Gault&Millau 2026; Cannes Tourism; Official restaurant website; Local dining guides

description: Aux Bons Enfants is a family-run Cannes institution near Marché Forville, open since the 1930s and still rooted in Provençal market cooking. Its cash-only, old-school character is part of the appeal rather than a weakness. It is one of the clearest informal local favorites for an affluent diner who wants real Cannes instead of another polished hotel room.
highlights: Beloved four-generation Provençal institution near Marché Forville, known for market produce and old-school character.
sources: Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand; Gault&Millau 2026; Official restaurant website; Local dining guides

description: Le Pompon is a modern bistro near the heart of Cannes, appreciated for small plates, market cooking and a curated wine sensibility. It is relaxed enough to sit outside the luxury core, but it has the taste level and local credibility that affluent diners often seek on a quieter night. The mood is contemporary, adult and more insider than tourist-brochure Cannes.
highlights: Modern local bistro with thoughtful small plates, market produce and an appealing wine-led rhythm.
sources: Michelin Guide; Gault&Millau 2026; Eater; Official restaurant website

description: Da Laura is a long-running Italian favorite near the station, founded in the early 1990s and still loved by locals, regular visitors and film-week diners. The appeal is not formality, but warmth, Piedmontese-inflected cooking and a reliably convivial room. It gives the Cannes set one relaxed, culturally embedded Italian option that still feels relevant to a sophisticated traveler.
highlights: Beloved central Italian institution with a loyal local and international following since the early 1990s.
sources: Eater; Condé Nast Traveler; Local dining guides

description: Fred l'Écailler is the protected Pointe Croisette seafood classic in the Cannes set, known for fish, shellfish and a loyal local-and-film-week following. It is relaxed rather than formal, but its producer-led seafood and peninsula history make it meaningful to an affluent diner seeking a culturally grounded night.
highlights: Pointe Croisette seafood classic with local fish, shellfish, a loyal following and old-school Riviera informality.
sources: Eater; Condé Nast Traveler; Official restaurant website
